title: Set 304

sentences.ko: 살이 6파운드쯤 빠졌는데, 거기서 자신감이 붙어서 햄버거 하나쯤은 괜찮겠지 했거든. 근데 그 하나가 일주일 내내 매일 햄버거가 돼 버렸어. 그래서 뭐, 다시 원점이야.
sentences.text: I'd lost like six pounds, and then I got cocky and figured one burger wouldn't hurt, but one burger turned into burgers every day for a week, so yeah, I'm back to square one.

alts.text: Lost like six pounds, got cocky, figured one burger's fine, and then it was burgers every day for a week. So yeah, back to square one.
I had lost about six pounds, but then I became overconfident and assumed one burger would not hurt. That one burger turned into burgers every day for a week, so I am back where I started.

sentences.note: **back to square one** 은 애써 한 게 다 날아가고 처음으로 돌아갔다는 뜻이에요. **got cocky** 는 일이 좀 잘되니까 우쭐해서 방심했다는 말이에요.

sentences.ko: 이번엔 진짜 배울 줄 알고 기타를 샀는데, 첫 주에 손가락이 너무 아파서 자꾸 미뤘어. 지금은 그냥 구석에 세워져 있는데 볼 때마다 괜히 찔려.
sentences.text: I bought a guitar because I really thought I'd finally learn, but my fingers hurt so much the first week that I kept putting it off, and now it's just sitting in the corner making me feel guilty.

alts.text: Got a guitar since I was sure I'd finally learn, but my fingers hurt so bad the first week I kept putting it off. Now it's just sitting in the corner guilt-tripping me.

I purchased a guitar because I truly believed I would finally learn to play, but my fingers were so sore during the first week that I kept postponing it, and now it simply sits in the corner and makes me feel guilty.

sentences.note: **putting it off** 는 해야 할 일을 자꾸 뒤로 미룬다는 뜻이에요. casual 에 나온 **guilt-tripping** 은 죄책감이 들게 만든다는 말이에요.

sentences.ko: 그 드라마 진짜 좋아했는데, 아빠 캐릭터를 죽여 버린 뒤로는 예전 같지가 않더라. 그래서 지난 시즌 중간쯤부터 그냥 안 보게 됐어.
sentences.text: I used to love that show, but after they killed off the dad, it just wasn't the same, so I kind of stopped watching halfway through last season.

alts.text: Loved that show, but once they killed off the dad, it just wasn't the same. Kinda stopped watching halfway through last season.
I used to enjoy that series very much, but after they killed off the father, it was no longer the same, so I stopped watching halfway through last season.

sentences.note: **killed off** 는 작가가 등장인물을 극 중에서 죽여서 하차시킨다는 뜻이에요. **it just wasn't the same** 은 예전만 못했다, 그 맛이 안 났다는 말이에요.

sentences.ko: 걔가 오늘 뭐 했는지 알아? 회의에서 내가 뽑은 숫자를 자기가 생각해 낸 것처럼 발표하더라. 근데 상사가 바로 거기 앉아 있어서 아무 말도 못 했어.
sentences.text: You know what he did today? He presented my numbers at the meeting like he came up with them himself, and I couldn't say anything because our boss was sitting right there.

alts.text: Guess what he did today? Presented my numbers at the meeting like they were his idea, and I couldn't say a thing since our boss was right there.
Do you know what he did today? He presented my figures at the meeting as though he had come up with them himself, and I was unable to say anything because our manager was sitting right there.

sentences.note: **You know what he did today?** 는 하소연을 꺼낼 때 흔히 쓰는 말이에요. **came up with** 는 아이디어나 답을 생각해 냈다는 뜻이에요.
sentences.situation: 회사 사람 때문에 짜증난 걸 친구한테 털어놓기

sentences.ko: 내 폰이 배터리가 40퍼센트쯤 남았다고 나와도 자꾸 꺼져서, 계속 충전기에 꽂아 둬야 돼. 이거 더 심해지면 새로 하나 사야 할 것 같아.
sentences.text: My phone keeps dying even when it says it's at like forty percent, so I have to keep it plugged in all the time, and if it gets any worse, I guess I'm going to have to get a new one.

alts.text: Phone keeps dying even at like forty percent, so it's gotta stay plugged in all the time. If it gets any worse, I guess I'm gonna need a new one.
My phone continues to shut off even when the battery shows about forty percent, so I must keep it plugged in at all times, and if the problem gets any worse, I suppose I will have to buy a new one.

sentences.note: **keeps dying** 은 휴대폰 같은 기기가 자꾸 꺼진다는 뜻이에요. **plugged in** 은 충전기나 콘센트에 꽂혀 있는 상태를 말해요.

reviewed: 3번 한국어 '아빠를 죽이고 나서는'은 누가 누구를 죽였는지 헷갈려서, 작가가 아빠 캐릭터를 하차시킨 뜻이 드러나게 '아빠 캐릭터를 죽여 버린 뒤로는'으로 고침
4번 한국어 '내가 낸 수치'가 어색해서 친구한테 하는 말투인 '내가 뽑은 숫자'로 고침
5번 formal의 'if it becomes any worse'는 원어민이 잘 안 쓰는 말이라 'if the problem gets any worse'로 고침
